page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column, with a running head at the top. Page number 58 at top right. A marginal note at the right, beside the paragraph on Illyrian. Gathering signature "H 2" at the foot.

main_text.p: quæ non ab hominibus literatis ita scribi possit, ut intelligatur: nam & nostra memoria primùm Rhætica alpina scribi coepit.
¶ Hvni vel Hvnni, vide in Hungaris.
¶ IACOBITAE in lingua Græca similibus characteribus utuntur, qui à Græcis parum variant, & nonnulli ejs peculiares adduntur. Postellus.

¶ ILLYRICA lingua Illyricisque literis utuntur Muschovitæ, sicuti & Slavi, Dalmatæ, Bohemi, Poloni & Lithuani.Illyrica li gua oms- ninm ld- tissima. Ea lingua longè omnium latissima esse perhibetur: nam Constantinopoli Ottomanorum in aula familiaris est, & nuper in Ægypto apud Memphiticum Sultanum & equites Mamaluchos haud ingratis auribus audiebatur. In hanc linguam ingens multitudo sacrorum librorum, industriâ maximè sancti Hieronymi & Cyrilli translata est. Præter quoque patrios annales, Alexandri etiam Magni Romanorumque Cæsarum, itemque M. Antonii & Cleopatræ memoriam iisdem literis commendatam tenent. Philosophiam verò & sideralem scientiam, cæterasque disciplinas, & rationalem medicinam nunquam attigere, Paulus Iovius.

page.notes: The marginal note at the right is set in small type over several short lines with hyphens; I have read it as "Illyrica / li gua oms- / ninm ld- / tissima." and the words are doubtful, especially "oms-", "ninm" and "ld-" (probably "omnium" and "latissima"). The word "ejs" in the Iacobitae paragraph is doubtful and may be "ejs" or "eys" [?]. The printed long s has been written as plain s throughout. The running head and page number are read at top right. The left edge is partly dark, so letters at the start of lines may be misread.
